Scale raster covariates and retain original-scale metadata

Source: R/convenience_funcs.R
scale_covariates.Rd

Transforms each layer of a SpatRaster and stores the original-scale offset and divisor as a "terradish_scale" attribute. When the scaled raster is used to build a conductance_surface, marginal-association plots (plot(fit, type = "marginal", data = surface)) can automatically back-transform x-axes to the original covariate units.

Usage

scale_covariates(
  covariates,
  method = c("zscore", "minmax"),
  center = TRUE,
  scale = TRUE,
  reference = NULL
)

Arguments

covariates

A SpatRaster or PackedSpatRaster whose layers should be scaled.

method

Scaling method applied to each layer independently. "zscore" (default) subtracts the layer mean and divides by the standard deviation, giving zero mean and unit variance. "minmax" maps the minimum to 0 and the maximum to 1.

center

Logical. Only used when method = "zscore". If TRUE (default), subtract the layer mean before dividing by the standard deviation.

scale

Logical. Only used when method = "zscore". If TRUE (default), divide by the layer standard deviation. If FALSE with center = TRUE, layers are centered but not divided.

reference

A previous scaled raster or its terradish_scale attribute. Applies the stored centers and scales by layer name instead of estimating new values. When supplied, method, center, and scale do not change the stored transformation.

Value

A SpatRaster with transformed values and a "terradish_scale" attribute.

Details

Scaling is strongly recommended before fitting conductance models. In the loglinear model, conductance is \(\exp(\theta \cdot x)\). When x has a large range (e.g. altitude in meters), a small change in \(\theta\) produces enormous conductance differences, making the objective surface poorly conditioned and the optimizer slow to converge.

Missing values (NA) are excluded from the computation of the mean, standard deviation, minimum, and range, and are left as NA in the output.

If a layer is constant (all values identical), the scale is set to 1 to avoid division by zero; the layer is then returned unchanged (or centered to 0 if center = TRUE).

The "terradish_scale" attribute is a named list with one element per layer; each element is a named numeric vector with entries center and scale (the subtracted offset and the divisor, respectively). crop_to_focal_buffer and conductance_surface preserve this attribute.

Name the layers before scaling. The stored centers and scales are keyed by layer name, so renaming a raster after scaling leaves stale names in the "terradish_scale" attribute and breaks back-transformation.

See also

scale_to_0_1, conductance_surface

Other graph setup: conductance_surface(), crop_to_focal_buffer()

Examples

library(terra)
r <- c(terra::rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, vals = c(100, 200, 300, NA)),
       terra::rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, vals = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.4, NA)))
names(r) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")

scaled_r <- scale_covariates(r)
attr(scaled_r, "terradish_scale")  # per-layer center and scale
#> $altitude
#> center  scale 
#>    200    100 
#> 
#> $forestcover
#>    center     scale 
#> 0.3666667 0.1527525 
#> 

# min-max scaling to [0, 1]
scaled_mm <- scale_covariates(r, method = "minmax")

# Preserve the training transformation on new values, matched by layer name.
new_scaled <- scale_covariates(r + 10, reference = scaled_r)
terra::values(new_scaled)
#>      altitude forestcover
#> [1,]     -0.9    64.37428
#> [2,]      0.1    66.33824
#> [3,]      1.1    65.68358
#> [4,]       NA          NA
# Values can fall outside the training range; they are not re-centered.
